title: Standing Cyclotron targets run without arbitrary request or item quotas
description:
As a publication operator, I want a configured standing Cyclotron target to accept ongoing decisions and unique source items without arbitrary lifetime, per-day request, or total-item quotas, so that monitoring continues until actual service or physical resource constraints require backpressure.

Feature: Standing publication targets are not quota-limited
  Scenario: Requests continue past former per-day and lifetime ceilings
    Given a standing publication target with the former total and per-day request ceilings
    When its usage exceeds those configured values
    Then eligible decisions continue through the existing guarded queue and request ledger
    And usage accounting continues to record requests and provider usage
  Scenario: Unique items are admitted beyond the former total item ceiling
    Given a standing target that has registered the former maximum number of unique items
    When a new valid unique item arrives
    Then it is registered idempotently without an arbitrary item-cap refusal
  Scenario: Real resource protections still provide backpressure
    Given a standing target whose bounded storage journal or per-item payload reaches its technical limit
    When an item is processed
    Then existing validation, concurrency, retries, fault handling, and storage protections remain effective
    And the refusal identifies the actual technical limit rather than a configured quota.

Definition of Done: remove standing-target total/per-day request quota and total unique-item capacity from trusted target configuration and runtime enforcement. Preserve the request ledger, measured usage, bounded request shape, queue/work batching, retries, concurrency, idempotency, and actual storage protections. Update hosted-publications docs, parameters/examples and tests. No deployment or live classification.
